### Ermenegildo Zegna Group Q3 2026 Revenues1 up 9% With Solid Growth Across All Regions and Continued Strength in the DTC Channel (+13% YoY)


10/22/2026


- **Q3 2026 Group revenues increased +8.9% year-on-year (YoY) to €433.8 million (+8.2% on an organic basis2).**


- **By Brand: ZEGNA brand revenues rose to €283.8 million, +13.8% YoY and +12.7% organic. Thom Browne revenues were €45.4 million, -5.9% YoY and -7.4% organic. TOM FORD FASHION revenues grew +5.4% YoY to €69.6 million (+5.5% organic).**
- **By Channel: DTC3 grew to €335.3 million, +13.0% YoY and +11.4% organic, driven by ZEGNA’s ongoing solid momentum across all regions. ZEGNA DTC rose +18.2% YoY and +16.4% organic.**
- **By Geography: all regions delivered solid growth, led by the Americas with +14.0% YoY (+13.6% organic) and the Greater China Region posting +8.7% YoY (+5.7% organic).**


- **9M 2026 Group revenues reached €1,421.1 million, +7.2% YoY and +8.9% organic.**


MILAN--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Ermenegildo Zegna N.V. (NYSE:ZGN) (the “Company” and, together with its consolidated subsidiaries, the “Ermenegildo Zegna Group” or the “Group”) today announced unaudited revenues of €1,421.1 million in the first nine months of 2026, up 7.2% YoY from €1,325.9 million in the same period of 2025 (+8.9% organic). In the third quarter, revenues reached €433.8 million, +8.9% YoY (+8.2% organic).


Ermenegildo “Gildo” Zegna, Executive Chairman of the Ermenegildo Zegna Group, commented: “This was another quarter of solid progress for our Group. Direct-to-Consumer continued to drive our growth, led by ZEGNA, which delivered a robust 16% organic increase in the DTC channel. I am also pleased with our Group’s performance across all regions. In particular, the Americas continued their double-digit trend despite an increasingly demanding comparison base, and the Greater China Region delivered steady growth in a quarter where the environment proved more challenging. ZEGNA led the way in all regions.


As we enter the final months of the year, we look ahead with cautious confidence. While the global environment remains uncertain, we stay focused on what has always set us apart: our close relationships with our clients grounded in more than a century of craftsmanship.”

In 9M 2026, revenues for the **ZEGNA** **brand** were €918.4 million, compared to €819.8 million in 9M 2025, (+12.0% YoY and +13.5% organic). In Q3 the brand reported revenues of €283.8 million, compared to €249.4 million in Q3 2025 (+13.8% YoY and +12.7% organic) driven by strong DTC organic growth across all regions.


In 9M 2026, revenues for the **Thom Browne brand** amounted to €168.5 million, compared to €177.4 million in 9M 2025 (-5.0% YoY and -2.2% organic). In Q3, the brand reported €45.4 million, compared to €48.2 million in Q3 2025 (-5.9% YoY and -7.4% organic), mainly reflecting the more challenging consumer environment in Greater China Region and the ongoing streamlining of the wholesale channel.


In 9M 2026, revenues for **TOM FORD FASHION (TFF)** amounted to €226.4 million, compared to €218.7 million in 9M 2025 (+3.5% YoY and +6.1% organic). In Q3, the brand reached revenues of €69.6 million from €66.0 million in Q3 2025 (+5.4% YoY and +5.5% organic), with both channels contributing positively.


**Textile** revenues were €97.9 million in 9M 2026, compared to €96.9 million in 9M 2025 (+1.0% YoY and +1.4% organic), with Q3 at +3.5% YoY and +5.0% organic. **Other** revenues were €9.9 million in 9M 2026, compared to €13.1 million in 9M 2025 (-24.4% YoY and -24.1% organic).

**DTC Revenues Analysis**


In 9M 2026, Group DTC revenues were €1,118.1 million compared to €994.7 million in 9M 2025 (+12.4% YoY and +14.4% organic). In Q3 the channel reported +13.0% YoY and +11.4% organic growth, driven by the ZEGNA brand.


**ZEGNA DTC** revenues grew +15.0% YoY and +16.3% organic in 9M 2026. In Q3, DTC revenues reported a growth of +18.2% YoY and +16.4% organic, driven by strong organic growth in all the regions. In particular, the Americas continued to outperform the overall performance of the channel. The Middle East region improved sequentially, delivering double-digit growth in the quarter. The Greater China Region (GCR) remained solid for the brand notwithstanding the slowdown in the industry in this area. At the end of September, ZEGNA counted 275 Directly Operated Stores (DOS), with 4 net closures in Q3 2026.


**Thom Browne DTC** revenues were up +6.3% YoY and +10.4% organic in 9M 2026. In Q3, DTC revenues reported a decline of -4.9% YoY and -6.6% organic, which suffered from a slowdown in demand in some key regions, including the GCR. At the end of September, Thom Browne counted 129 DOS, with one net opening in Q3, including a store in Shanghai Plaza 66.


**TOM FORD FASHION DTC** revenues were up +5.5% YoY and +8.9% organic in 9M 2026. In Q3, DTC revenues grew +4.7% YoY and +4.2% organic, driven by a positive performance in the Americas, EMEA and the Rest of APAC. At the end of September, TOM FORD FASHION counted 67 DOS, unchanged compared to the end of June.


**Wholesale Branded Revenues Analysis**


In 9M 2026, wholesale branded revenues were €195.2 million, compared to €221.2 million in 9M 2025 (-11.8% YoY and -10.4% organic). In Q3, wholesale branded revenues were €63.4 million, -5.2% YoY and -3.8% organic. However, as wholesale is driven by seasonal deliveries, the year-to-date (YTD) trend provides a more meaningful indication of performance than quarterly performance, which can be affected by shifts in delivery timing.


**ZEGNA wholesale** revenues were €96.6 million in 9M 2026 (-8.0% YoY and -5.7% organic), with Q3 down -9.8% YoY and -7.9% organic. The performance reflects the Company’s decision to preserve exclusivity and reduce its exposure to this channel, particularly for its iconic products.


**Thom Browne wholesale** revenues were €29.4 million in 9M 2026 (-36.8% YoY and -36.5% organic) with Q3 at -9.9% YoY and -10.7% organic, as a result of the continuous streamlining of the wholesale channel carried out by the brand.


**TOM FORD FASHION wholesale** revenues were €69.2 million in 9M 2026 (-0.8% YoY and +0.1% organic), with a positive Q3 at +7.2% YoY and +8.9% organic driven by the good reception of Fall Winter collections.

In 9M 2026, **EMEA** recorded revenues of €491.4 million (+2.4% YoY and +3.0% organic), representing 35% of the Group’s revenues. In Q3 2026, EMEA recorded +6.9% YoY and +6.3% organic growth, driven by double-digit growth at ZEGNA, partially offset by negative wholesale performance at Thom Browne and TOM FORD FASHION. The Middle East region delivered a strong sequential improvement in the quarter.


In 9M 2026, revenues in the **Americas** amounted to €440.7 million (+14.7% YoY and +17.8% organic), representing 31% of the Group’s revenues. In Q3 2026, the region reported a growth of +14.0% YoY and +13.6% organic, with ZEGNA leading with double-digit growth in the DTC channel, partially offset by a negative performance in the ZEGNA wholesale channel. TOM FORD FASHION also delivered solid growth in the region.


In 9M 2026, the **GCR** recorded revenues of €320.2 million (+6.6% YoY and +6.5% organic), representing 22% of the Group’s revenues. In Q3 2026, GCR revenues increased by +8.7% YoY and +5.7% organic, driven by ZEGNA’s DTC channel, partially offset by the negative performance at Thom Browne.


In 9M 2026, revenues in the **Rest of APAC** reached €166.9 million (+4.9% YoY and +10.9% organic), representing 12% of the Group’s revenues. Q3 2026 revenues increased by +3.6% YoY and +5.0% organic, with ZEGNA and TFF contributing positively while Thom Browne performed broadly in line with last year despite the more challenging environment in Korea and Japan.

**About Ermenegildo Zegna Group**


Founded in 1910 in Trivero, Italy, the Ermenegildo Zegna Group (NYSE:ZGN) is a global luxury company with a leading position in the high-end menswear business. Through its three complementary brands, the Group reaches a wide range of communities and market segments across the high-end fashion industry, from ZEGNA’s timeless luxury to the modern tailoring of Thom Browne, to seductive elegance with TOM FORD FASHION. The Ermenegildo Zegna Group is internationally recognized for its unique Filiera, owned and controlled by the Group, which is made up of the finest Italian textile producers fully integrated with unique luxury manufacturing capabilities, to ensure superior excellence, quality and innovation capacity. The Ermenegildo Zegna Group has more than 7,200 employees and recorded revenues of €1.92 billion in 2025.

**Non-IFRS Financial Measures**


The Group’s management monitors and evaluates operating and financial performance using several non-IFRS financial measures including: revenues on a constant currency basis (Constant Currency) and revenues on an organic growth basis (organic or organic growth). The Group’s management believes that these non-IFRS financial measures provide useful and relevant information regarding the Group’s financial performance and financial condition, and improve the ability of management and investors to assess and compare the financial performance and financial position of the Group with those of other companies. They also provide comparable measures that facilitate management’s ability to identify operational trends, as well as make decisions regarding future spending, resource allocations and other strategic and operational decisions. While similar measures are widely used in the industry in which the Group operates, the financial measures that the Group uses may not be comparable to other similarly named measures used by other companies nor are they intended to be substitutes for measures of financial performance or financial position as prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards. A definition, explanation of relevance and a reconciliation of each non-IFRS financial measure to the most directly comparable measure calculated and presented in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards are set out below.


**Revenues on a constant currency basis (Constant Currency)**


In addition to presenting our revenues on a current currency basis, we also present certain revenue information on a constant currency basis (Constant Currency), which excludes the effects of foreign currency translation from our subsidiaries with functional currencies different from the Euro.


We calculate Constant Currency revenues by applying the current period average foreign currency exchange rates to translate prior period revenues of foreign subsidiaries expressed in local functional currencies different than the Euro.


We use revenues on a Constant Currency basis to analyze how our underlying revenues have changed between periods independent of the effects of foreign currency translation.


Revenues on a Constant Currency basis are not a substitute for revenues on a current currency basis or any IFRS-related measures, however we believe that revenues excluding the impact of foreign currency translation provide additional useful information to management and to investors in analyzing and evaluating our revenues and operating performance.


**Revenues on an organic growth basis (organic or organic growth)**


In addition to presenting our revenues on a current currency basis, we also present certain revenue information on an organic growth basis (organic or organic growth). Organic growth is calculated as the change in revenues from period to period, excluding the effects of (a) foreign exchange and (b) acquisitions and disposals.


In calculating organic growth, the following adjustments are made to revenues:


1. Foreign exchange – Current period average foreign currency exchange rates are used to translate prior period revenues of foreign subsidiaries expressed in local functional currencies different than the Euro.
2. Acquisitions and disposals – Revenues generated by businesses and operations acquired in the current year are excluded. Revenues generated by businesses and operations acquired in the prior year are excluded from the current year for the same period that corresponds to the pre-acquisition period in the prior year. Additionally, where a business or operation was a customer prior to an acquisition, the related pre-acquisition revenues are excluded from the current and prior periods. Revenues generated by businesses and operations disposed of in the current year or prior year are excluded from both periods as applicable.


We believe the presentation of revenues on an organic basis is useful to better understand and analyze the underlying change in the Group’s revenues from period to period on a consistent perimeter and constant currency basis.


Revenues on an organic basis are not a substitute for revenues on a current currency basis or any IFRS-related measures, however we believe that revenues excluding the effects of (a) foreign exchange and (b) acquisitions and disposals provide additional useful information to management and to investors in analyzing and evaluating our revenues and operating performance.
